title: Column and row comparison for uniformly bounded-below integer bicomplexes
statement: Let C be an abelian category with countable coproducts and let f:K to L be a map of integer cochain bicomplexes [def-sp-double-complex-total]. Suppose common integers P,Q satisfy K^{p,q}=L^{p,q}=0 whenever p

source.place: Tags 012X, 0132 and 0133; finite-diagonal comparison by truncation

proof.text: Fix a total homology degree n and put M=n-Q+1. The projection to the outer stupid truncation at M is an isomorphism in total degrees n-1,n,n+1: a removed summand has p>M and hence q<Q. Prove this summandwise using GradedObject.isIso_mapMap_apply and the zero-object isomorphism criterion. It follows that the projection is a quasi-isomorphism at n.

The truncated bicomplexes have only finitely many nonzero columns P through M. Column maps remain quasi-isomorphisms by the retained-column projection isomorphisms. Apply the source library theorem total.quasiIso_map_of_finitely_many_columns, totalize the naturality square of projections, and apply two-out-of-three at n.
For rows apply the preceding statement to flipped bicomplexes and conjugate by totalFlipIso. Naturality follows on each total summand from the signed total-flip formulas.
